text: I have been a family physician for twenty-two years, and I can tell you that the opioid crisis is the worst public health disaster I have witnessed in my career. I have lost patients — good people with families and careers — to addiction that started with a legitimate prescription for back pain. This is not a matter of personal weakness. The pharmaceutical companies knew these drugs were highly addictive and marketed them aggressively to doctors like me. I changed my prescribing practices years ago, and I think the medical profession as a whole has a responsibility to reckon honestly with its role in this epidemic.
